question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Washout time course with acute degron depletion
ideas.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then after washout acutely degrade JUN/FOS (dTAG/AID) at different delays, measuring retention of chromatin accessibility (ATAC) and transcriptional responsiveness. If accessibility persists without AP-1, it was only needed for establishment; if it collapses, AP-1 actively maintains memory.

ideas.title: Priming and re-stimulation hysteresis assay
ideas.description: Vary the number, duration, and spacing of stimulus pulses and measure the magnitude and kinetics of the second response (nascent RNA, e.g., PRO-seq) in primed versus naive cells. Test whether the enhanced response depends on AP-1 using A-FOS expressed only during priming versus only during recall.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-traced multiome
ideas.description: Use barcoded clones or sister-cell pairing with joint scRNA/scATAC to test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression states are shared among related cells beyond what is expected by chance after stimulus removal. Compare concordance across divisions to quantify heritability and its decay.

ideas.title: Live imaging of endogenous AP-1 reporters across divisions
ideas.description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN and a target-gene reporter, then track mother-daughter lineages by time-lapse to see whether activity states persist through mitosis and across generations. Pair with mitotic CUT&RUN to test whether AP-1 bookmarks chromatin.

ideas.title: Motif editing and dCas9 tethering at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs at primed enhancers to test necessity for persistent accessibility and faster recall, and conversely tether AP-1 or its pioneer domain via dCas9 to naive loci to test sufficiency to establish a heritable open state. Read out with ATAC, H3K27ac and reporter expression over weeks.

candidates: Time-course ChIP/CUT&RUN of AP-1 (FOS/JUN) after transient stimulus and washout
ATAC-seq of AP-1 motif accessibility at days after stimulus removal
Acute degron (dTAG/AID) depletion of JUN/FOS after stimulus to test maintenance of accessibility
Optogenetic pulse of AP-1 activity with long-term tracking of target gene expression
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) lineage-traced clones to test heritability of AP-1 states
Live imaging of endogenous FOS-GFP reporter across cell divisions in mother-daughter pairs
Mitotic bookmarking assay: AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes by live imaging and CUT&RUN
Dose/duration-dependence: vary stimulus pulse number and measure persistence of response (hysteresis)
Re-stimulation assay: primed vs naive cells measuring faster/stronger transcription (memory of prior exposure)
Dominant-negative (A-FOS) induced at different times after priming
CRISPR deletion/mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers
dCas9-based forced tethering of AP-1 at a locus to test sufficiency for establishing memory
Histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) with and without AP-1 loss after priming
Hi-C/Micro-C to assess AP-1-dependent loop persistence after stimulus
Mathematical modeling of AP-1 feedback loops (bistability) fitted to single-cell time series
Phosphorylation state (JNK/ERK) tracking vs AP-1 occupancy to separate signaling persistence from chromatin memory
In vivo inflammation/injury model with tissue-resident cells re-challenged weeks later, with AP-1 perturbation
Pioneer activity test: nucleosome occupancy changes by MNase/footprinting at AP-1 sites after priming
Proteomic turnover/FRAP measurements of AP-1 residence time and protein half-life
Cross-cell-type comparison of AP-1 composition (dimer identity) in primed states using ChIP-exchange or CUT&Tag
